newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei sold off in thin, volatile market.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei sold off in thin, volatile market.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures were sharply sold off in late Thursday trade as the market's failure to breach a key resistance level prompted players to reverse track, dealers said.

After a deceptively upbeat start, which saw the benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract hit a high of 18,400, the market was sold down by Japanese houses, ending at 17,900, down 440 points. Turnover was a thin 14,300 lots.
Dealers said the market's recent volatility, where 500-point swings have become standard fare, made it difficult to trade.
"People are generally still prepared to sell the Nikkei. It was struggling to get to 18,500 and every time it falters, they sell it down," said a trader with a European futures house.
He said there was no news or fresh leads on the underlying cash market and the dollar's weaker stance against the yen did not provide any clear signals.
"The closer we get to the financial year end, the greater the level of unofficial government support there'll be (for the Nikkei)," he said.
"But until it really clears back up to 18,500, we're not going to be out of the woods," he said, noting that the March Nikkei was still within a broader 17,200-18,400 range.
The March MSCI Taiwan index contract ended up 0.7 from its open, at 310.7 on 168 lots. April was at 310.6 on 129 lots.
"We should be able to hold above the 310.0 level going into the Lunar New Year. There's good underlying support on the cash market," said a trader at a local house.
